title: The Infinite State
author: Richard Swan
review:
Swan's best book yet. I've read all of his published fantasy books and have really liked to loved each of them and I actually applied for the ARC for Infinite State and was denied (maybe after being lukewarm on Steel Gods lol). I was fairly skeptical about him doing sci-fi but this book has a wonderful balance of great characters, exciting plot, and a well built world. It also has a lot of great ideas and political intrigue.

This is the coolest blend of a sci-fi dystopia ala 1984 and something like Star Wars that's just a really fun space opera adventure story. This improves on a lot of the classic sci-fi dystopia books because people are actually living in that world the best they can while being actively oppressed and surveiled constantly; where a wrong world or thought is instant death.

I thought the ending of this was simultaneously satisfying while also I'm looking forward to reading the next one, which is soon (next year) because Swan is a writing machine. He's one of my most reliable authors and I enjoy picking up whatever he comes out with almost immediately on release.
